runners_data.name: Steal A Glance
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who should get uncontested lead and dictate the pace throughout

races.paceDynamic: Steal A Glance will lead this contest from the flag and set a sustainable pace without pressure from the largely prominent and hold-up field. Lady Kara and Likewhatyousee may track closely as the main prominent runners, but with Dancing Dame, Medina Blue, and Doobeedee all preferring to come from behind, the early pace will be measured. The lack of early pressure allows the leader to dictate terms and potentially kick clear at the business end. This race shape clearly favours the early pace-setter and any prominent runners who can stay close enough to challenge, as the hold-up horses will face a difficult task against a controlled tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Stays Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Steal A Glance gets an easy lead and kicks clear approaching the last hurdle
scenarios.body: The sustainable pace allows the front-runner to maintain energy reserves for a decisive move, while the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground against controlled fractions. Prominent runners who stayed close enough have the best chance to respond.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Takeover
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Kara or Likewhatyousee can track the leader closely and produce a stronger finishing kick
scenarios.body: The measured early pace helps these prominent runners conserve energy while staying within striking distance, allowing them to exploit their tactical positioning. They can time their challenge perfectly as Steal A Glance begins to tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes even slower than expected and the hold-up horses get perfect splits in the straight
scenarios.body: Dancing Dame and Medina Blue could benefit from an exceptionally pedestrian gallop that allows them to unleash their finishing speed. However, they still face the challenge of making up significant ground against positioned rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Steal A Glance goes too slowly early and multiple horses converge simultaneously approaching the final flight
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where class and form rather than running style determines the outcome. This scenario requires the leader to misjudge the pace completely.

watchPoints.text: Steal A Glance could steal this if allowed to dictate a soft pace without early pressure from the field
Lady Kara's ability to stay close enough to the leader will determine if she can mount an effective challenge
Dancing Dame and other hold-up horses need to see frantic early pace to have realistic winning chances
Doobeedee's 225-day layoff combined with known finishing problems makes her a risky proposition despite Harry Fry's training
The going report shows consistent Good conditions across all races, eliminating ground as a variable for tactical planning

races.name: William Hill Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Groom De Cotte
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with recent winning form who should benefit from the likely sprint finish, though 10-year-old legs may lack the sharpest kick.

runners_data.name: Jack's Jury
runners_data.note: Another hold-up type who has been running well in similar company and carries the trainer's best recent form with 3 places from last 4 starts.

runners_data.name: Final Entry
runners_data.note: David Pipe charge who may have to make his own running given his prominent tendencies, but 51-day break could leave him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Winning Paddy
runners_data.note: Light weight and recent winner who could prove dangerous if allowed to coast into the race, though modest rating suggests limited scope.

runners_data.name: Hurst Hill
runners_data.note: Consistent sort who may inherit the lead by default, but trainer's 2-from-9 recent record raises questions about current stable form.

runners_data.name: Bits Ballou
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner carrying bottom weight, but Sam Twiston-Davies booking suggests connections see improvement coming after 33-day freshener.

races.paceDynamic: With all six runners showing hold-up tendencies and no confirmed front runner, this race will drift into a crawling early pace with plenty of shuffling for position. The lack of natural pace-setters means someone like Hurst Hill or Final Entry may reluctantly take it up, but they'll go no faster than they have to. The field will bunch up turning for home before exploding into a sprint finish over the final 3-4 furlongs. This tactical setup strongly favours horses with a sharp turn of foot and tactical speed - those who can quicken fastest when the real racing begins.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crawling Pace Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If no horse commits to making the running early and they go very slowly to halfway
scenarios.body: The field compresses into a tight bunch with 4f to run, creating a cavalry charge finish that rewards the sharpest acceleration. Horses with class and a killer kick thrive when the pace collapses completely.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Gallop Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Hurst Hill or Final Entry takes responsibility and maintains an even tempo throughout
scenarios.body: The race develops into a true test of stamina over this extended trip, suiting horses who stay strongly rather than those dependent on sprint finishes. The consistent pace plays to genuine stayers who can grind it out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid Race Injection
scenarios.trigger: If someone injects pace from the 2-mile mark to string the field out
scenarios.body: The increased tempo creates gaps and makes it a more searching test, favouring horses who combine stamina with tactical speed. Those caught flat-footed by the move struggle to get back into contention.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Breakaway Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If one horse goes clear early and the field allows them too much rope
scenarios.body: The leaders get into an uncatchable rhythm while the pack plays follow-the-leader, creating a front-running shock. Only applies if the field shows complete tactical naivety.

watchPoints.text: Watch for any horse that shows early intent to dominate - with no natural pace-setter, whoever takes responsibility could steal a decisive advantage.
Monitor the pace through the first mile - if it's genuinely crawling, expect a bunched field and potential interference in the home straight.
Keep an eye on Groom De Cotte's jumping rhythm - as the oldest horse in the field, any signs of laboured jumping could signal vulnerability.
Watch Final Entry's fitness levels given the 51-day layoff in what could become a stamina test if the pace is honest.
Observe whether Winning Paddy can maintain his recent winning momentum stepping up significantly in class from his last victory.

races.name: Olympus Plant & Tool Hire Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Linden Lane
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner whose hold-up style suits the likely tactical scenario, though 34-day break and 168lbs burden are concerns in a sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Crab Road
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a dangerous habit of fading in the finish, making him vulnerable if this becomes the expected cavalry charge.

runners_data.name: Ask Peter
runners_data.note: Solid each-way claims with consistent hold-up form, though the 64-day layoff and 10-pound jockey allowance create mixed signals.

runners_data.name: Coup De Gold
runners_data.note: Lightest burden at 157lbs but the 237-day absence is a significant negative despite connections showing faith with the booking.

runners_data.name: Blue Siam
runners_data.note: Recent 13-day turnaround suggests connections are happy with current form, and the 156lbs mark looks workable for a 4-year-old.

runners_data.name: Minnie Belle
runners_data.note: Bottom weight of 149lbs is a major tactical advantage in the expected sprint finish, though overall form figures remain moderate.

races.paceDynamic: With all six runners showing hold-up tendencies and no confirmed front runner, this race will likely drift into a muddling early pace. Linden Lane and Ask Peter, both carrying higher weights, may find themselves forced into more prominent positions by default, creating a tactical vacuum early. The lack of natural pace-setters will compress the field and create a bunched finish where positioning at the final hurdle becomes critical. This race shape strongly favours horses with a sharp turn of foot and those who can quickest exploit the inevitable sprint finish that will develop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bunched Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If no horse takes the initiative early and the pace remains steady throughout
scenarios.body: The field stays tightly packed turning for home, creating a cavalry charge finish where the lightest-weighted horses with the best recent form can quickest exploit gaps. Blue Siam and Minnie Belle benefit from their featherweight burdens in the final surge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Linden Lane Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Linden Lane's connections decide to make use of her class advantage early
scenarios.body: The OR 89-rated mare dictates terms from the front, using her superior rating to stretch the field and expose the moderate opposition. Her proven stamina over this trip allows her to sustain pressure where others weaken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Long Layoff Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If Coup De Gold's 237-day absence shows despite her low weight advantage
scenarios.body: The veteran mare finds the pace too sharp after her lengthy break, while others who've had recent runs can respond better to the tempo changes. Recent form becomes the decisive factor over theoretical ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so pedestrian that the race becomes a pure lottery in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Jockey tactics become paramount as positioning at the last hurdle determines everything, with Crab Road's tendency to fade in the finish proving costly despite his decent rating. The most alert pilot gets first run on their mount.

watchPoints.text: Crab Road's finishing kick - his tendency to fade late could be exposed badly in a bunched finish where sustained effort is required.
Early pace development - if Linden Lane or Ask Peter don't take it up, this could become pedestrian and turn into a pure lottery.
Blue Siam's jumping fluency on quick turnaround - any hesitation at hurdles will be costly in a tightly-bunched field.
Coup De Gold's fitness levels after 237 days off - any signs of blowing or struggling to go the pace will end her chances early.
Jockey positioning at the final hurdle - with all six hold-up performers, the pilot who gets first run will have a decisive advantage.

runners_data.note: Front running style suits small field but 9-day break might leave him short of peak fitness

runners_data.name: Donnie Azoff
runners_data.note: Hold-up style needs slow pace to be effective, proven course winner with headgear back on

runners_data.name: Dream Diamond
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with question marks over 39-day absence and headgear change to hood

runners_data.name: Siam Park
runners_data.note: Prominent style but inconsistent recent form including fall, 5lb claimer reduces burden

runners_data.name: Almuhit
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer with top jockey booking and quick 2-day turnaround

runners_data.name: Three Pikes
runners_data.note: Non-runner

races.paceDynamic: Morning Mayhem will likely take them along from the front in this small field, with Dream Diamond, Siam Park, and Almuhit all capable of tracking close behind given their prominent tendencies. With only one confirmed front runner and multiple prominent racers, the pace should be steady rather than frantic, allowing the leaders to dictate terms without excessive pressure. Donnie Azoff represents the sole hold-up threat but will need the pace to collapse to be effective from the rear. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and front runners who can position handily and kick from a good position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Morning Mayhem gets an uncontested lead and the prominent horses don't press early
scenarios.body: The pace becomes pedestrian allowing the leader to control the race from pillar to post. Front runners and early prominent horses benefit from the lack of early pressure and can save energy for a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Diamond, Almuhit and Siam Park all race keenly and press Morning Mayhem
scenarios.body: A genuine speed battle develops between the prominent racers, creating a true test of stamina. This favours the horse with the best finishing kick from a handy position, potentially setting up Donnie Azoff's hold-up style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and Donnie Azoff gets a perfect trip tracking the leaders
scenarios.body: The veteran can exploit his proven ability to quicken off a slow pace. His recent second at this course gives him a tactical edge if the race unfolds to suit his patient style.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Morning Mayhem goes too fast early under pressure and the field comes back to him dramatically
scenarios.body: The early leaders pay for their exertions and the race becomes a sprint finish between whoever has been held up. This creates chaos where any horse finding a clear run can capitalize on the pace bias.

watchPoints.text: Morning Mayhem's early pace-setting - if he goes too fast early he could set up the race for closers
Donnie Azoff's positioning through the early stages - needs to be closer than usual given the small field
Dream Diamond's jumping rhythm after 39 days off - any early mistakes could compromise his prominent position
Siam Park's confidence after recent fall - watch for any hesitancy at the obstacles
The overall pace through the first mile - if genuinely slow it transforms the finish dynamics completely

races.name: St. Austell Brewery Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: La Pinsonniere
runners_data.note: Likely pace-setter with class edge but 34 days off and recent disappointing effort at Cheltenham raises fitness questions.

runners_data.name: Court In A Storm
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form with cheekpieces applied, Kim Bailey's 15-day gap suggests readiness for this step up in trip.

runners_data.name: Rickety Bridge
runners_data.note: Another prominent type fresh from back-to-back wins, Paul Nicholls excels with horses in this form cycle.

runners_data.name: Dexperts Opinion
runners_data.note: Will race prominently off bottom weight, Mickey Bowen's 12.5% strike rate and recent win suggests confidence despite lower grade.

races.paceDynamic: La Pinsonniere will likely dictate from the front in this small field, with Court In A Storm, Rickety Bridge, and Dexperts Opinion all having prominent tendencies but none guaranteed to press early. The pace should be sustainable rather than frenetic with only four runners spread across 3m2f, allowing La Pinsonniere to control tempo without significant early pressure. With no confirmed hold-up horses and the extended trip, this sets up as a test of stamina and jumping rather than tactical speed. This race shape favours horses who can travel prominently and have the stamina reserves to respond when the pace lifts approaching the business end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Leader
scenarios.trigger: If La Pinsonniere gets an easy lead without early pressure from the prominent runners
scenarios.body: She can dictate comfortable fractions and use her class advantage when others come under pressure. Her Henderson training and de Boinville partnership excels in these tactical situations.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Court In A Storm and Rickety Bridge track La Pinsonniere closely from early stages
scenarios.body: The pace becomes more honest throughout, suiting horses with proven stamina over the trip. Court In A Storm's recent winning form and Rickety Bridge's back-to-back wins suggest both have the engine for this test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady early but quickens significantly from three furlongs out
scenarios.body: The extended trip becomes crucial and recent form over similar distances matters most. Rickety Bridge's consecutive wins at this sort of trip give him the fitness edge over less battle-hardened rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If all four track each other conservatively until the final half-mile
scenarios.body: It becomes a sprint finish where class tells and fresher horses benefit from the tactical nature. La Pinsonniere's superior rating and Dexperts Opinion's recent winning momentum could prove decisive.

watchPoints.text: If La Pinsonniere looks laboured jumping the early fences, her 34-day absence and recent poor Cheltenham run could signal bigger problems.
Watch Court In A Storm's jumping rhythm early as cheekpieces are a new addition and any mistakes will hurt prominent position.
Monitor how aggressively Rickety Bridge and Dexperts Opinion position early, as both could press La Pinsonniere if connections are confident.
Look for any horse tracking wider than expected as the good going offers multiple racing lines on this course.

races.paceDynamic: At The Oche is listed as non-runner, removing the confirmed front runner from this small field. First Angel and Beorma both show prominent tendencies and will likely dispute the early lead, with Cobbler's Boy held up in rear. Without At The Oche's sustained pace-setting, this becomes a tactical affair where the two prominent runners may go steadier early before quickening. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can control the tempo and have enough left to resist the hold-up challenge of Cobbler's Boy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Beorma Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Beorma takes charge early and dictates a steady pace
scenarios.body: His recent winning streak shows he's in peak form and can quicken off his own pace. Cobbler's Boy faces a tough task giving weight and making up ground in a slowly-run race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: First Angel Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If First Angel's freshness tells after 87 days off
scenarios.body: The veteran could benefit from his break and trainer Martin Keighley's 1/7 strike rate suggests selective placement. His prominent style suits if he can find his old form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If both prominent runners go too steady early
scenarios.body: A cat-and-mouse affair develops where neither wants to make the running, setting up Cobbler's Boy's hold-up style perfectly. Dan Skelton's 12/38 record provides confidence in the tactical ride.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Beorma Wins Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Beorma faces no early pressure from First Angel
scenarios.body: He can cruise through steady fractions and prove too classy in the finish. His five-race winning streak and excellent going record make him hard to oppose.

First Angel's fitness after 87-day layoff could be crucial to his prominent racing style
Cobbler's Boy needs the pace to collapse to be effective from his hold-up position
Small field dynamics may not develop enough pace for hold-up horses to be effective
